prompt: Isometric technical cutaway illustration of a home network split in two. An unbranded matte router sits on a plywood shelf in a utility closet at centre-left; thin cable lines run from it two ways: one passes through a raised partition gate to a flat-screen smart TV and a video doorbell on the low side, the other runs to a closed laptop and a document stack on the high side. The partition casts a long shadow across the shelf. Flat muted palette of graphite and bone white with a rust accent on the gate, thin consistent line weight over visible plywood grain, one directional light from the upper left. Wide 16:9 framing, router off-centre on the thirds, generous empty margin, unlabelled.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The article is an explainer of how a system works — a flat network redrawn into a guest network and a firewalled IoT VLAN — which is exactly the trigger for a technical isometric cutaway. An axonometric diagram with the router at a partition gate makes the boundary, not any single device, the hero, and it rotates the desk away from its recent photographic and collage treatments.
cue: A guest network is the floor
subject: An unbranded router on a utility-closet shelf routing cables through a firewall partition that separates a smart TV and doorbell from a laptop and document stack
core_thesis: A smart TV that nobody has signed into still phones ten outside brands in its first powered-on minute, so a home network must be redrawn — guest network as the floor, a firewalled IoT VLAN as the fix — because a device trusted with nothing sits inside a network trusted with everything.
core_conflict: The convenience of a flat home Wi-Fi, where every gadget can reach every other device, versus the trust boundary owners must build — keeping computers off the network their smart gear uses.
composition: Wide 16:9 isometric cutaway, router off-centre on the left third with the partition gate running through the frame, generous empty margin around the assembly
